findings.title: `validate frontmatter` ignores the resolved worktree and operates on the main checkout
findings.description:
Description: `validateFrontmatterAction` calls the worktree-aware `resolveProjectWorktree` (validate.ts:89) but destructures only `{ id }`, silently dropping `worktreeId`, then passes `project.projectPath` to `validateFrontmatterFiles` (validate.ts:99-101). `resolveProjectWorktree` deliberately sets `worktreeId` when the CWD is inside a registered worktree (see `findProjectByCwd` in packages/cli/src/utils/project.ts, `source: 'worktree'`). Every sibling file-scanning command in the CLI routes its path through `resolveOperationPath(project, worktreeId)` for exactly this reason — `plan.ts:43`, `task.ts:50,62,84`, `prompt.ts:52`, `arch.ts:53` all do; `check.ts:222` overlays per worktree. This command is the outlier.

Concrete effect: a user standing in a git worktree directory (no `--project`) resolves to the worktree's project, but the command then validates — and with `--fix`, **writes** — against `project.projectPath`, i.e. the main checkout. So `--fix` can mutate the main tree's `project-documents/user/...` while the operator believes they're working in the worktree. This is a real deviation from the established worktree-routing convention and a foot-gun on the destructive `--fix` path. Suggested fix: destructure `worktreeId` and use `resolveOperationPath(project, worktreeId) ?? project.projectPath`, matching the other commands. (No test exercises a worktree-CWD scenario, which is why it slipped through.)

findings.title: `--fix` (via the shared writer) stamps `dateUpdated` on machine-artifact docs
findings.description: Description: The new command reuses `updateFrontmatterField`, which unconditionally writes `dateUpdated: dateStamp` whenever the fixed key is not itself `dateUpdated` (markdownWriter.ts: `if (key !== 'dateUpdated') { setFrontmatterField(lines, closingIndex, 'dateUpdated', dateUpdated); }`). The #73 schemas for `review-resolution`/`gate-evidence`/`devlog` deliberately omit `dateUpdated`, with an explicit comment that the validator must not "manufacture a false claim by copying dateCreated into it." But when `--fix` corrects any other field on such a doc (e.g. a missing/invalid `dateCreated` or `docType`), the writer still injects `dateUpdated: <today>`, re-introducing exactly the field the design said these moment-snapshots shouldn't carry. This is pre-existing writer behavior (also shared by `cf check --fix`), so it's not introduced here — but the new command is the first path that realistically fixes these docTypes, and it's worth a follow-up: either the writer should skip the `dateUpdated` stamp for these docTypes, or the intent should be documented as accepted.

findings.title: `exitCode = 2` for setup errors is a new, undocumented convention
findings.description: Description: The refactor changes `handleError(err)` to `handleError(err, exitCode = 1)` and `validate` calls `handleError(err, 2)` (validate.ts:180) for setup errors (project not found / no projectPath), while `process.exitCode = 1` is used for validation findings. That's a sensible and, I think, intentional split for a script-oriented validator (2 = "couldn't even run" vs. 1 = "ran, found problems") — and it's covered by the "an unresolvable project exits 2" test. The default-param form is backward-compatible, so no other command's behavior changes. It's just a second exit-code meaning that appears in exactly one command and isn't mentioned in the command's help text; a one-line note in the `frontmatter` description ("setup errors exit 2; findings exit 1") would make the script contract explicit.

findings.title: Command and schema additions are well-typed and well tested
findings.description:
Description: Verified, not just asserted: the CLI test suite covers the meaningful paths — clean run (exit 0), findings without `--fix` (exit 1), unresolvable project (exit 2, via the `resolveProjectWorktree` throw path), `--fix` success (exit 0 + the #71/#73 date-stamp argument asserted against `updateFrontmatterField`), `--fix` failure (exit 1 + error surfaced), unfixable finding (stays unfixed, exit 1), JSON shape (`filesChecked`/`findings`/`errors`/`warnings`), JSON fix-mode fields (`fixed`/`fixLog`/`fixErrors`), and explicit-vs-undefined path forwarding. Tests are organized per the convention (centralized `tests/commands/`, centralized `tests/schema/`), mock external deps at the boundary (`vi.mock('@context-forge/core/node')`), and follow arrange-act-assert with one concept per test. The core schema tests correctly re-scope the "universal fields" and "status uses VALID_STATUSES" loops to the 8 canonical types so the new 3 docTypes don't trip them, and add positive/negative/alias cases for each new docType. No `any`, discriminated-union-friendly types, and `printHumanOutput`/`groupByFile` are clean and correctly handle the no-`fixAction` case (no spurious "Fixed" line, since a fix log entry's `field` is always a string while an unfixable finding's `fixAction?.field` is `undefined`).

One deliberate design choice I confirmed is intentional and documented, not a defect: `--fix` here applies without a confirmation prompt, explicitly contrasted with `cf check --fix` in the command description ("findings are per-document and deterministic, and this command is meant for scripts") — reasonable given the narrower blast radius, and the no-worktree default case behaves correctly.

structured_findings.summary: `validate frontmatter` ignores the resolved worktree and operates on the main checkout
`--fix` (via the shared writer) stamps `dateUpdated` on machine-artifact docs
`exitCode = 2` for setup errors is a new, undocumented convention
Command and schema additions are well-typed and well tested
